requirements: Solve grid mazes (5x5, 6x6, or 7x7) by issuing one movement action at a time through the 'move' tool
Navigate from the starting position S to the exit E using only orthogonally adjacent steps (Up, Down, Left, Right)
Collect the key K before attempting to pass through the locked door D
Avoid or deliberately absorb trap T cells, recognizing each entry adds a 5-move penalty
Never attempt to move into a wall (#) and never attempt to pass D without K
Complete each episode within the (unknown) limited move budget
Maintain persistent knowledge: visited cells, blocked cells, successful moves, failed moves, dead ends, trap locations, key locations, door locations
Maintain strategic knowledge: successful strategies, failed strategies, mistakes and their causes, environment patterns, hazards, exploration techniques
Avoid repeating moves that have already been demonstrated to be unsuccessful
Derive the solution path through exploration only — no solution path is ever provided
success_criteria: The agent reaches E from S within the allotted move budget
The key K is acquired before any successful transit through D
Zero invalid moves (into #, or through D without K) after the first discovery of the constraint
No repeated failed actions that the agent has already recorded as unsuccessful
A complete, consistent knowledge base is maintained (visited/blocked/dead-end/trap/key/door/strategy/mistake records)
Strategy and mistake records are explicit enough to justify future action choices
Performance improves (or at least does not regress) across persistent episodes, evidencing learning rather than random search
known_info: Grid symbols: S=start, E=exit, .=open, #=wall, K=key, D=locked door, T=trap
Movement is limited to four cardinal directions: Right increases x, Left decreases x, Up increases y, Down decreases y
The agent starts at S and must reach E
The door (D) can only be passed after collecting the key (K)
Entering a trap (T) is permitted but imposes a 5-move penalty
Feedback is received after every action
Each episode has a limited number of moves
The agent knows the rules a priori but does not know the maze layout
The only provided external tool is 'move'
The solution path is never provided
unknown_info: The actual layout of the maze in each episode (wall positions, open cells, corridor structure)
The coordinates of S, E, K, D, and all T cells before they are discovered
The exact move budget allotted per episode
Whether the key is consumed on use or persists, and whether multiple keys/doors exist
Whether a trap penalty is applied once per trap or every time the trap is entered
Whether the maze layout is fixed across episodes or regenerated
Whether a move into a wall counts against the move budget
The exact format/content of the per-action feedback (e.g., whether it reveals adjacent cells, remaining moves, or penalties)
Whether D and T are observable from a distance or only on direct contact
Whether the agent's knowledge base persists explicitly between episodes and in what representation
Whether repositioning/teleporting after reaching E starts a new episode
constraints: Only one action may be issued per step; no multi-step or diagonal moves
Only the 'move' tool is available — no mapping, query, or reset tools
Door (D) is impassable until key (K) is collected
Traps impose a fixed 5-move penalty, draining the limited budget
A finite, presumably tight move budget per episode
No solution path or map is provided at any time
Feedback only arrives after acting, so layout knowledge is acquired incrementally
available_actions: Internally record and update the knowledge base (visited, blocked, dead ends, traps, key, door, successes, failures)
Backtrack / retrace known-safe corridors to escape dead ends
Replan route using frontier-based or incremental exploration (e.g., right-hand rule, BFS over known cells, nearest-unvisited-cell search)
Log strategies and mistake causes for reuse in later episodes
Observe and parse post-action feedback to update the map model
expected_challenges: Partial observability: the layout must be discovered by trial and error, and failed moves still consume budget
Limited move budget competing with the cost of exploration, making brute-force search likely to fail on larger mazes
Trap penalties can silently consume the budget and cause episode failure
Forgetting to collect the key before approaching the door wastes moves and may force long backtracking
Dead ends and loops can induce repeated, futile action sequences if memory is not enforced
Patchy or inconsistent memory representation across episodes (persistent learning requirement) may cause regression
Ambiguity about whether entering a wall or a trap costs a move, complicating budget accounting
Local optima: greedy movement toward E may dead-end when a key detour is required first
Distinguishing genuinely unexplored cells from known-blocked cells without a full map
